components.text: Explain why moral pronouncements are not merely emotive expressions or directives lacking truth value.
Address the distinction between expressing an attitude and truthfully reporting possession of that attitude.
Explain why ethical pronouncements are not merely emotive expressions or directives lacking truth value.
Address the distinction between expressing an attitude and truthfully reporting possession of that attitude.
Show that a factual landscape and scientific routes select an experiential destination rather than only describing available means.
Determine whether factual knowledge of experiential possibilities and routes supplies an evaluative destination or only means to a selected destination.
Explain whether subjective destination-setting remains exhaustive when the preferences selecting destinations are themselves causally alterable.
Address whether the preferences selecting experiential destinations can themselves be treated as fixed subjective endpoints.
Account for choosing preference alterations without relying on an independent evaluative standard beyond preference.
Explain how an agent can evaluate and voluntarily alter first-order preferences without relying on an independent moral standard.
Address whether a preference-only account fully handles agents who fail to recognize attainable improvements in life.
Answer the claim that evaluative language merely expresses attitudes or directives without truth value.
Address the claim that higher-order preference and scientific means exhaust the significance of possible experiential improvement.
Address whether refusing truth-apt normative language eliminates anything evaluatively significant.
Clarify whether objective facts about conscious systems amount to objective value or instead serve values located in those systems.
Clarify whether unrecognized experiential improvement establishes objective value or remains value relative to a conscious system.
Show why the reality of first-person appearances establishes objective value rather than merely real subjective experience.
Address whether the first-person or system-relative manifestation of value makes it merely subjective rather than a real feature facts can track.
Explain why granting increasingly pleasurable conscious experience still requires objective moral truth rather than a complete preference-based practical story.
Explain whether recognizing experiential reality requires objective moral truth rather than a complete preference-based practical account.
Address whether open-minded discovery of better experiences can be explained without objective normative language.
Address whether preference change can proceed through voluntary exploration and increasing satisfaction.
Show what objective evaluative role remains after preference, cooperation, discovery, and instrumental science are granted.
Explain why better and worse experiential navigation is more than objective means serving a subjectively selected destination.
Explain why objective facts about conscious outcomes establish objective value rather than merely system-relative effectiveness.
Identify what objectively evaluative guidance adds to a preference-based practical account of flourishing, cooperation, and discovery.
Address whether objectively discoverable routes provide only instrumental means or also identify better practical directions.
Address whether better outcomes remain merely relative to subjective values of conscious systems.
